claims.text: LPBF or DED can fabricate refractory high-entropy alloys from Group IV-V transition metals.
Rapid solidification during LPBF or DED produces a non-equilibrium ultrafine-grained microstructure.
A homogenization anneal at 1200-1400°C dissolves segregation and precipitates in the proposed RHEA.
A subsequent aging treatment below 600°C can control interstitial distribution without excessive grain growth.
Processing under inert gas or vacuum minimizes additional oxygen, nitrogen, and carbon uptake.
LPBF followed by homogenization will yield a single-phase BCC microstructure with ultrafine grains.
The processed BCC solid solution will retain a high density of dislocations.
Rapid cooling during LPBF or DED suppresses brittle TCP-phase formation and promotes a metastable single-phase BCC structure.
The processing route suppresses brittle B2-phase formation.
Aging can sequester interstitial atoms at dislocation cores or precipitate them as stable, non-brittle carbides or nitrides.
Low-temperature aging modifies electronic structure and may induce Jahn-Teller distortions that improve ductility.
Managing interstitials through aging prevents brittleness associated with high interstitial content.
The processed alloy will have a yield strength above 400 MPa at 1600°C.
The processed alloy will achieve room-temperature plastic strain above 2%.
Conventionally processed NbMoTaW and WTaMoNbV-type RHEAs are severely brittle at room temperature, with plastic strain below 0.2%.
The room-temperature brittleness of conventionally processed RHEAs is caused by interstitial impurities and insufficient microstructural refinement.
Vacuum-arc-melted WMoTaNbV can exhibit a single BCC high-entropy phase.
LPBF has been demonstrated for both MoNbTaW and WTaMoNbV.
Alloying intrinsically brittle Mo and W with Group IV or V transition metals can improve intrinsic ductility through composition-induced electronic-structure changes.
The proposed strategy may not apply to alloys containing substantial Al, Cr, Mo, or W because such additions favor B2 or Laves phases.

contradictions.description: The proposed family is restricted to Group IV-V elements and the boundary excludes significant Group VI content, but NbMoTaW, WTaMoNbV, and NbMoTaW are repeatedly used as representative alloys or test compositions even though Mo and W are Group VI elements.
The target is described as a single-phase BCC microstructure, while the mediator also permits precipitation of carbides or nitrides, which would make the resulting microstructure multiphase.

The hypothesis attributes ultrafine grains to the final homogenized state, but the route includes a 1200-1400°C anneal and provides no grain-stabilization mechanism showing that ultrafine grains would survive that treatment.
